title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's motivic or Galois-theoretic material. It is page 44 of an older French typescript in Bourbaki/Cartan style on analytic functions of several complex variables, almost certainly scrap paper reused for the 1965 notes; the neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on norms, 'catégories de Dennis/Deuring' and gerbes. The page continues a proof of the homotopy invariance of the integral of a closed differential form ω = Σ_k f_k dx_k whose coefficients are locally sums of convergent power series.

Setting: φ: I×J → C^n (I=[a,b], J=[c,d]) is a continuous homotopy between paths γ = φ(·,c) and γ' = φ(·,d). The compact set φ(I×J) is covered by finitely many polycylinders P_i on which each f_k is a convergent power series centred at a_i.

Step 1 (Lebesgue-number argument). Let δ(x) be the largest distance from x to the boundary (complement) of those P_i that contain x. δ is continuous and positive, so it attains a minimum ρ > 0 on the compact image. Hence every open polycylinder of radius ρ centred on a point of φ(I×J) lies in some P_i. There each f_k re-expands as a power series in z_j − x_j (re-centring, chap. I §1 prop. 4).

Step 2 (subdivision). Uniform continuity gives ε with ||φ(t,s) − φ(t',s')|| ≤ ρ/4 whenever |t−t'|, |s−s'| ≤ ε. Subdivide I by points t_α and J by points s_β with mesh ≤ ε. For 1 ≤ β ≤ q−1, let γ_β be the polygonal path through the points φ(t_α, s_β); set γ_0 = γ and γ_q = γ'. It suffices to show ∫_{γ_β} ω = ∫_{γ_{β+1}} ω.

Step 3 (local step, completed on the next typed page). For each α, the arcs of γ_β and γ_{β+1} over [t_α, t_{α+1}] lie in one polycylinder Q_{α,β} of radius ρ. On Q_{α,β}, ω has a primitive, by the Poincaré lemma for closed forms with power-series coefficients. Summing the differences of primitives over α telescopes to zero.

This is the standard proof that integrals of closed analytic 1-forms, and hence analytic continuation, are invariant under homotopy with fixed endpoints.
errors: The parametrisation formula has a typo, present in the typescript itself: the denominator should be t_{α+1} − t_α, not t_{α+1} − t.

Minor point: 'distance aux frontières' should be read as distance to the complement of P_i. With that reading δ is a maximum of finitely many Lipschitz functions, each extended by 0 outside P_i, and is therefore continuous, as claimed.

The argument implicitly needs ρ/4 small enough that the four corner images and the connecting segments (or arcs of γ, γ') lie in a single polycylinder of radius ρ. This holds by convexity in the sup norm, so there is no real gap.

ideas.what: Homotopy invariance of integrals of closed analytic 1-forms, proved via a Lebesgue-number and grid-subdivision argument with local primitives on polycylinders
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy form of Cauchy's theorem / monodromy theorem for closed 1-forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cauchy, Weierstrass, Poincaré); textbook versions in H. Cartan, Bourbaki
ideas.where_published: Standard textbooks (e.g. H. Cartan, Théorie élémentaire des fonctions analytiques); not a Grothendieck text

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reused page of a routine typescript on elementary several-variable complex analysis, unrelated to the motivic notes around it. Its only interest is archival: it shows Grothendieck wrote on the back of old typescripts.
transcription_corrections: The denominator 't_{α+1} − t' faithfully reflects the typescript, but it is a typo for t_{α+1} − t_α.
'de rayon ρ' and 'de rayons ρ' both appear in the original; this is harmless.
